observations.title: The inventory accounts were overstated by a net amount of P32.595 million due to accounting errors in record keeping, non-maintenance of inventory records and unreconciled records of the Office of the City Accountant (OCAT) and City General Services Office (CGSO) contrary to Paragraph 27 of the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) 1. This condition weighed on the fairness of the presentation of the inventories in the Financial Statement (FS).
observations.description:

The Drug and Medicines; Medical, Dental and Laboratory Supplies; Textbooks and Instructional Materials Inventory; and Other Supplies and Materials totaling P1,140,655,093.28 accounted for 86 per cent of these inventories (Table 1).

1.3 The City recognizes inventories delivered directly to the end users as already issued, thus, expensed outright. It takes up the inventories physically counted by the CGSO and end-users at year-end and accordingly adjust the inventories expensed outright.

1.4 We have also noted instances of deliveries at year-end which are recognized as inventories together with the setting up of the corresponding payable accounts. Once the documentation of the deliveries to end users is completed, these inventories are expensed.

1.5 Comparative analysis of the carrying amounts of the inventory accounts per books of accounts and those physically counted showed inexistent inventories totaling P35,521,926.90 (Table 2). This overstated the inventory accounts by as much and shows ineffective inventory reconciliation between the OCAT and CGSO.

1.6 The accounting errors came about mainly because of deficiencies in record keeping.

1.6.1 The Stock Cards (SCs) prepared and maintained by the CGSO are incomplete and not properly accomplished. The SCs have no beginning balances but contains only the quantities of the items issued and remaining balance at a certain period. The relevant information in the AIR, Purchase Order, Delivery Receipts and the corresponding Requisition and Issue Slip are not captured in the SC (e.g., item description, date received and date issued were not recorded in the SCs).

1.6.2 Instead of maintaining one SC for each class of item, the CGSO prepares another separate SC for subsequent deliveries for similar procured items. This poses difficulty in tracking the movements of each item of inventory. At any one time, one cannot readily establish the availability of inventory items.

1.6.3 We have further noted that OCAT does not maintain the Supplies Ledger Cards and Procurement Received Journal.

1.6.4 The foregoing record-keeping deficiencies prevent the OCAT and CGSO from effectively and efficiently tracking the movements of inventories, reconciling their records and timely detecting and correcting the errors in accounting for the movements of inventories.

1.7 The foregoing accounting errors weighed on the fairness of the presentation of the inventories in the FS contrary to Paragraph 27 of the IPSAS 1.

recommendations.label: a.
recommendations.text: OCAT correct the accounting errors in record-keeping; and
recommendations.lead_in: We recommended and Management agreed that:

recommendations.label: b.
recommendations.text: OCAT and CGSO: (a) maintain the prescribed inventory records and information that will enable effective and efficient tracking of the movements of inventories; and (b) reconcile their inventory records periodically.

observations.description:

3.2 The foregoing balances consist of AP from CYs 2021 to 2022 but without complete supporting schedules/breakdown. The prior year payables account for P2,015,171,468.42 or 39.68 per cent of the AP balances as of December 31, 2022. Individual ledgers for each creditor/claimant for CY 2021 transactions were not maintained and submitted as of April 24, 2023. The schedule of AP submitted by OCAT was a summary schedule per fund indicating only the account code, the class of expenditure like Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) and Capital Outlay (CO), and total amount per year. In particular, this made confirmation of payable balances very inefficient and arduous.

3.3 This limited to a great extent the test of details of these payables, thus, foregoing the benefit of early detection and correction of errors.

3.4 This accounting deficiency is contrary to Section 12 (Appendix 8), Volume II of the GAM for LGUs, which requires that details such as Nature of Account/Address/Contact Person/Number - name of the individual/company/ agency and office address of debtor/creditor shall be indicated in the SL. In case of an agency/company, include the contact person and telephone number/e-mail address, etc. This also works against the standard accounting control of adequate documentation of transaction and events that provides adequate audit trail.

observations.title: The City has not implemented 43 out of the total 188 essential Gender and Development (GAD) Programs/Projects/Activities (PPAs) contrary to Philippine Commission on Women (PCW), Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG), Department of Budget and Management (DBM) and National Economic Development Authority (NEDA) Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2013-01 dated July 18, 2013, thus, bypassed the timely realization of the benefits expected therefrom.
observations.description:
5.1 Item C.8 of PCW-DILG-DBM-NEDA JMC No. 2013-01 dated July 18, 2013 or the Guidelines on the Localization of the Magna Carta of Women, provides the guidelines on the preparation and submission of LGU GAD Accomplishment Reports (AR), such as:

(1) The GAD Focal Point System (GFPS) shall prepare their annual GAD AR based on the DILG-approved GAD Plan and Budget (GPB) or the enacted GPB following the form prescribed in Annex E. Activities completed until the end of the year may be included in the final LGU GAD AR.

5.2 Section 4.1.C.7.4 of the same JMC also provides that the GFPS shall regularly monitor if the GAD budget is being spent for what it was intended for and check on the actual cost of implementing the GAD activities.

5.3 Further, Section 6.1 of PCW-DILG-DBM-NEDA Joint Circular No. 2016-01 amending Section 4.1.C.7.1 of PCW-DILG-DBM-NEDA Joint Circular No. 2013-01 states that the Local Chief Executive shall issue an appropriate policy directive, copy furnished the DILG Office that conducted the review of the LGU GPB, to disseminate and implement GPB.

5.4 Review of the GPB submitted to the Audit Team on January 18, 2023 disclosed that the City allocated the amount of P1,130,942,111.54 or 5.09 per cent of the total appropriation from the regular sources amounting to P22,200,000,000.00 for CY 2022, thus, compliant with the Magna Carta for Women. observations.title: The City has not remitted P393.564 million representing the amounts withheld as of December 31, 2022 for the accounts of the BIR, GSIS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth, contrary to the appertaining legal prescriptions.
observations.section_heading: COMPLIANCE WITH TAX LAWS AND OTHER REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS / Due to Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth
observations.description:
6.1 Inter-Agency Payables are contributions due to/collections received/amounts withheld for remittance to the different government agencies. In the case of the City, these are payables to BIR, GSIS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth.

6.2 Our audit of these accounts is guided by the following legal provisions:

Withholding and Remittance to BIR:

Executive Order No. 651 dated February 16, 1981 requires government offices, agencies and instrumentalities to comply strictly with the law and regulations in the withholding and remittance of internal revenue taxes imposed by the National Internal Revenue Code.

BIR Revenue Regulation (RR) No. 2-98, as amended, and RR No. 4-2002, as amended, require the remittance of withheld taxes within 10 days following the end of the month the withholding was made.

Withholding and Remittance to GSIS:

Section 6 of RA No. 8291 or The GSIS Act of 1997 provides the guidelines in the collection and remittance of employee-members’ contributions.

Related thereto, COA issued Circular No. 2016-007 dated March 7, 2016 on the audit of GSIS premium deductions and remittances which was reiterated and extended to include audit of payments for GSIS monthly salary deductions and other loan amortization under COA Memorandum No. 2017-015 dated August 8, 2017.

Withholding and Remittance to Pag-IBIG:

Section 23 (a) of RA No. 9679 also known as An Act Further Strengthening the Home Development Mutual Fund, and for Other Purposes provides that it shall be the duty of every employer, private or public, to set aside and remit the contributions required under this Act in accordance with the mechanism determined by the Board of Trustees.

Withholding and Remittance to PhilHealth:

Section 11 of National Health Insurance Act of 2013 as amended by RA No. 9241 requires that the remittance of contribution shall be mandatory for all members. It shall be made to PhilHealth offices or to any of the accredited collecting agents. Failure to timely remit the appropriate premium contribution shall be subject to interest and penalties as prescribed by the Corporation without prejudice to other applicable penalties herein provided.

6.3 Analysis of the Inter-Agency Payables account as of December 31, 2022 showed that the City has not remitted P393,563,558.43 to the BIR, GSIS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth contrary to the foregoing legal prescriptions. (Table 9)

recommendations.text: We reiterated our recommendation that Management direct the OCAT and CTO to remit the P393.564 million to the BIR, GSIS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth without further delay.

observations.management_comment: 6.6 The Management commented that the remaining amounts due to the GSIS were actually being remitted but rejected by the GSIS Electronic Billing and Collection (GEBS) and considered as clarificatory items (clarif). Clarificatory items were due to the salary rates, name, Business Partner number and responsibility code which did not match with the records in the GEBS. As a result, the GEBS did not generate the Summary of Totals which serves as the order of payment. Accordingly, the OCAT has returned the schedule of remittances to the concerned offices of the City for corrections.
